20_25_13: A trustworthy messenger is, to the ones who sent him, like snow's coolness amid the heat of harvest — he brings their very souls back to life.
20_25_14: Like clouds and wind without rain is one who boasts of gifts he never gives.
20_25_15: By patience a ruler is won over, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
20_25_16: Have you found honey? Eat only what is enough for you, lest you be glutted with it and vomit it up.
20_25_17: Let your foot be rarely in your neighbor's house, lest he grow weary of you and hate you.
20_25_18: Like a war-club, a sword, and a sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbor.
20_25_19: Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in the day of trouble.
20_25_20: Like one who takes off a garment on a cold day, like vinegar poured on soda, is the one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
20_25_21: Should the one who hates you go hungry, set bread before him to eat; should he be parched, hand him water to drink.
20_25_22: For by doing so you rake burning coals together upon his head, and the LORD Himself will repay you.
20_25_23: The north wind brings forth rain, and a secretive tongue, angry faces.
20_25_24: It is better to live in a corner of the housetop than in a shared house with a quarrelsome wife.
20_25_25: Like cold water to a thirsty soul is good news from a far country.
20_25_26: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
20_25_27: It is not good to eat too much honey; so to search out one's own glory is no glory.
20_25_28: Like a city broken open and left without walls is a man who has no rule over his own spirit.
20_26_1: Like snow in the heat of summer or rain at harvest time, so honor is altogether unfitting for a fool.
20_26_2: Like a sparrow in restless flitting or a swallow in its darting, so an undeserved curse never lands.
20_26_3: What the whip is to the horse and the bridle to the donkey, the rod is to the back of fools.
20_26_4: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will become just like him.
20_26_5: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.
20_26_6: Whoever sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks down violence.
20_26_7: Like the legs of a lame man that dangle useless, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
20_26_8: Like binding a stone fast in a sling, so is the giving of honor to a fool.
20_26_9: Like a thornbush brandished in the hand of a drunkard, so is a proverb in the mouth of fools.
20_26_10: Like an archer who wounds everyone at random, so is he who hires a fool or hires any passerby.
20_26_11: As a dog goes back to its own vomit, so a fool repeats his folly again and again.
20_26_12: Have you ever met a man convinced of his own wisdom? Even a fool stands a better chance than he does.
20_26_13: The sluggard says, 'There's a lion in the road! A lion is prowling the open streets!'
20_26_14: As a door turns on its hinges, so the sluggard turns over on his bed.
20_26_15: Having sunk his hand down into the bowl, the sluggard finds the journey back to his mouth too exhausting to finish.
20_26_16: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with sound judgment.
20_26_17: Like grabbing a passing dog by the ears is the man who meddles in a quarrel that is none of his own.
20_26_18: Like a madman flinging deadly firebrands, arrows, and death,
20_26_19: so is the man who deceives his neighbor and then says, 'I was only joking!'
20_26_20: For lack of wood the fire goes out, and where there is no whisperer, strife falls silent.
20_26_21: As charcoal is to embers and wood is to fire, so a quarrelsome man is for kindling strife.
20_26_22: The words of a whisperer are like dainty morsels; they slide down into the innermost chambers of the body.
20_26_23: Like a glaze of silver dross over a clay pot are fervent lips joined to an evil heart.
20_26_24: The one who hates disguises himself with his lips, but inside he harbors deceit;
20_26_25: When his voice turns gracious, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.
20_26_26: Though his hatred is masked by deceit, his wickedness will be laid bare before the whole assembly.
20_26_27: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and the one who rolls a stone — it rolls back upon him.
20_26_28: A lying tongue hates the very ones it crushes, and a flattering mouth brings on ruin.
20_27_1: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a single day may bring to birth.
20_27_2: Let the praise of you rise from another's mouth, never from your own; let a stranger speak it, never your own lips.
20_27_3: A stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool's provocation outweighs them both.
20_27_4: Wrath is cruel and anger an overwhelming flood — but who can stand before jealousy?
20_27_5: Better an open rebuke than love that hides itself.
20_27_6: Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are lavish and false.
20_27_7: The well-fed soul tramples on honey, but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
20_27_8: Like a bird that strays far from its nest is a man who strays from his place.
20_27_9: Oil and incense gladden the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is his counsel from the soul.
20_27_10: Do not forsake your own friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house in the day of your calamity — better a neighbor near than a brother far away.
20_27_11: Be wise, my son, and gladden my heart, that I may have an answer for the one who taunts me.
20_27_12: The prudent man sees danger coming and takes cover, but the simple keep walking and pay the price.
20_27_13: Seize the coat of one who pledges himself for a stranger, and hold it as security when he stands surety for a foreign woman.
20_27_14: Whoever blesses his neighbor with a booming voice, rising up early in the morning, will have it counted to him as a curse.
20_27_15: A constant dripping on a day of steady rain and a quarrelsome wife are one and the same.
20_27_16: To restrain her is to restrain the wind, or to grasp oil with the right hand.
20_27_17: Iron is sharpened by iron, and one man sharpens the face of his friend.
20_27_18: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever guards his master will be honored.
20_27_19: As water mirrors face to face, so a man's heart reveals the man.
20_27_20: Sheol and Abaddon are never full, and the eyes of man are never satisfied.
20_27_21: The crucible tests silver and the furnace gold, and a man is tested by the praise he receives.
20_27_22: Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle, among the crushed grain, his folly will not leave him.
20_27_23: Know well the condition of your flocks, and set your heart upon your herds.
20_27_24: For riches do not last forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.
20_27_25: When the grass is gone and the new growth appears, and the herbs of the hills are gathered in,
20_27_26: The lambs will clothe you, and the goats will buy you a field;
20_27_27: and there will be goats' milk enough for your own food, for the food of your household, and to sustain the life of your servant girls.
20_28_1: The wicked flee though no one gives chase, but the righteous are bold as a lion.
20_28_2: When a land rebels, its rulers are many; but under a man of understanding and knowledge, order is kept and endures.
20_28_3: A poor man who crushes the poor is like a driving rain that beats down the crops and leaves no bread.
20_28_4: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep it take their stand against them.
20_28_5: Justice stays hidden from men bent on evil, but to all who search after the LORD its whole meaning lies open.
20_28_6: Better is a poor man who walks in his integrity than a rich man whose ways are crooked.
20_28_7: Whoever guards the law is a discerning son, but a companion of gluttons brings shame to his father.
20_28_8: Whoever swells his wealth by interest and extortion gathers it up for one who will be kind to the poor.
20_28_9: If a man turns a deaf ear to the law, even his prayer is detestable.
20_28_10: Whoever leads the upright astray into an evil path will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit good.
20_28_11: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees right through him.
20_28_12: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise to power, men go into hiding.
20_28_13: He who hides his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them will find mercy.
20_28_14: Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but whoever hardens his heart will fall into ruin.
20_28_15: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
20_28_16: A ruler who lacks understanding is a cruel oppressor, but he who hates unjust gain will lengthen his days.
20_28_17: A man weighed down by the guilt of bloodshed will be a fugitive to the grave; let no one hold him back.
20_28_18: Whoever walks blamelessly will be kept safe, but the man of crooked ways will fall all at once.
20_28_19: Whoever works his land will have plenty of bread, but whoever chases empty schemes will have his fill of poverty.
20_28_20: A faithful man will overflow with blessings, but whoever rushes to get rich will not go unpunished.
20_28_21: To show partiality is not good, yet for a mere crust of bread a man will do wrong.
20_28_22: A stingy man scrambles after wealth and never knows that want is on its way to him.
20_28_23: Whoever rebukes a man will in the end find more favor than the one who flatters with his tongue.
20_28_24: Whoever robs his father or mother and says, 'It is no sin,' is a partner to the destroyer.
20_28_25: A greedy heart stirs up strife, but whoever trusts in the LORD will be enriched.
20_28_26: Whoever trusts in his own heart is a fool, but whoever walks in wisdom will be kept safe.
20_28_27: Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing, but whoever shuts his eyes to them will gather many curses.
20_28_28: When the wicked rise to power, men go into hiding; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
20_29_1: A man who, after much reproof, only stiffens his neck will be shattered in an instant — and beyond all healing.
20_29_2: When the righteous grow many and great, the people rejoice; but when a wicked man rules, the people groan.
20_29_3: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of harlots squanders his wealth.
20_29_4: By justice a king gives his land a firm foundation, but a man greedy for bribes tears it down.
20_29_5: A man who flatters his neighbor is spreading a net for his own feet.
20_29_6: An evil man is trapped in the snare of his own sin, but the righteous runs ahead singing and glad.
20_29_7: The righteous takes up the cause of the poor; the wicked has no mind even to understand it.
20_29_8: Scoffers set a city ablaze, but the wise turn back wrath.
20_29_9: When a wise man takes a fool to court, the fool only rages or laughs, and there is no settling it.
20_29_10: Bloodthirsty men hate the blameless, but the upright seek to guard his life.
20_29_11: A fool lets out his whole temper, but a wise man holds it back and stills it within.
20_29_12: If a ruler gives ear to lies, all his officials turn wicked.
20_29_13: Set the destitute beside the man who preys on him, and one thing binds them together — it is the LORD who kindles light in the eyes of both alike.
20_29_14: A king who judges the poor with faithfulness — his throne will stand firm forever.
20_29_15: The rod and reproof give wisdom, but a child left to himself shames his mother.
20_29_16: When the wicked grow many, so does transgression; but the righteous will look upon their downfall.
20_29_17: Correct your son, and he will give you rest; yes, he will bring delight to your soul.
20_29_18: Where there is no vision from God, the people throw off all restraint; but blessed is the one who keeps the law.
20_29_19: A servant is not corrected by words alone; for though he understands, he will not respond.
20_29_20: Do you see a man hasty with his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
20_29_21: Pamper a servant from his youth, and in the end he will turn out ungrateful and grasping.
20_29_22: An angry man stirs up strife, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.
20_29_23: A man's pride will bring him low, but the humble in spirit will lay hold of honor.
20_29_24: Whoever shares with a thief hates his own life; he hears the curse laid down, yet says nothing.
20_29_25: The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
20_29_26: Many court the ruler's favor, but it is from the LORD that a man receives justice.
20_29_27: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and the one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
20_30_1: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh — the oracle. This man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and to Ucal:
20_30_2: Surely I am too brutish to be called a man, and I have not the understanding of a human being.
20_30_3: I have not learned wisdom, nor do I possess the knowledge of the Holy One.
20_30_4: Who has gone up to heaven and come down again? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of His hands? Who has bound the waters in a cloak? Who has set fast all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is His Son's name, if you know?
20_30_5: Every word of God is refined pure; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
20_30_6: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and you be exposed as a liar.
20_30_7: Two things I ask of You; do not withhold them from me before I die:
20_30_8: Keep falsehood and lying words far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches — feed me only with the bread that is my portion —
20_30_9: lest I be full and disown You and say, 'Who is the LORD?' or lest I be poor and steal, and so profane the name of my God.
20_30_10: Never carry a servant's name to his master with malice; if you do, his curse will fall back on you, and the guilt of it will be yours to carry.
20_30_11: There is a breed of men that curses its father and does not bless its mother;
20_30_12: a breed that is clean in its own eyes, yet is not washed of its filth;
20_30_13: a breed — how lofty are its eyes, how raised its haughty stare!
20_30_14: a breed whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, to devour the poor off the earth and the needy from among mankind.
20_30_15: The leech has two daughters, crying, 'Give! Give!' There are three things never satisfied, four that never say, 'Enough!':
20_30_16: the grave; the barren womb; the land never sated with water; and the fire that never says, 'Enough!'
20_30_17: The eye that mocks a father and scorns to obey a mother — the ravens of the valley will peck it out, and the young eagles will devour it.
20_30_18: Three things are too wonderful for me, four I cannot comprehend:
20_30_19: the way of an eagle in the sky; the way of a serpent on a rock; the way of a ship in the heart of the sea; and the way of a man with a maiden.
20_30_20: Such is how the adulteress goes about it: when she has finished, she dabs her mouth clean and protests, 'There is no wrong in anything I have done.'
20_30_21: There are three things that set the earth to shaking, and a fourth whose weight it has no strength to carry:
20_30_22: under a servant when he becomes king, and a fool when he is filled with food;
20_30_23: under an unloved woman when at last she is married, and a maidservant who dispossesses her mistress.
20_30_24: Four things on the earth are small, yet they are wise, made wise beyond the wise:
20_30_25: the ants are a people without strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;
20_30_26: the rock badgers, for all their weakness as a people, still set their dwellings deep within the cliffs;
20_30_27: the locusts have no king, yet they all go out in ranks;
20_30_28: the lizard you can grasp in your hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.
20_30_29: Three things are stately in their stride, four are stately in their going:
20_30_30: the lion, mightiest among beasts, who turns back before nothing;
20_30_31: the strutting rooster, the he-goat, and a king secure with his troops around him.
20_30_32: If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, or if you have schemed evil — clap your hand over your mouth.
20_30_33: For as pressing milk brings forth curds, and twisting the nose brings forth blood, so pressing out anger brings forth strife.
20_31_1: The words of King Lemuel — the weighty oracle his mother pressed upon him as she shaped him:
20_31_2: What shall I say, my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
20_31_3: Do not pour out your strength on women, nor your ways on those who bring kings to ruin.
20_31_4: It is not for kings, Lemuel — it is not for kings to be drinking wine, nor for rulers to crave strong drink.
20_31_5: Lest he drink, and forget what the law decrees, and twist the just cause of all the afflicted.
20_31_6: Give strong drink to the one perishing, and wine to those bitter in soul.
20_31_7: Let the cup loose him from his poverty, and let his weary toil press on his mind no longer.
20_31_8: Open your mouth for the voiceless, in the cause of all who are left to ruin.
20_31_9: Open your mouth, judge with righteousness, and defend the cause of the poor and the needy.
20_31_10: A woman of valor — who can find her? Her worth runs far beyond rubies.
20_31_11: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he will lack no gain.
20_31_12: She brings him good and never harm, all the days of her life.
20_31_13: She seeks out wool and flax, and works it with eager hands.
20_31_14: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from far away.
20_31_15: She rises while it is still night, sets food before her household, and assigns each servant girl her portion.
20_31_16: She sizes up a field and acquires it; from the earnings of her hands she plants a vineyard.
20_31_17: She girds her waist with strength and makes her arms strong for the work.
20_31_18: She knows her trading is good; her lamp does not go out at night.
20_31_19: She sets her hands to the distaff, and her palms grasp the spindle.
20_31_20: She opens her palm to the poor, and reaches out her hands to the needy.
20_31_21: She has no fear of the snow for her household, for all of them are clothed in scarlet.
20_31_22: She makes her own coverings; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
20_31_23: Her husband is known in the gates, when he takes his seat among the elders of the land.
20_31_24: She makes fine linen garments and sells them, and supplies sashes to the merchants.
20_31_25: Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the days to come.
20_31_26: She opens her mouth in wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue.
20_31_27: She keeps watch over the ways of her household, and never eats the bread of idleness.
20_31_28: Up rise her children to pronounce her blessed; her husband too lifts his voice in her praise:
20_31_29: 'Many daughters have done valiantly, but you surpass them all.'
20_31_30: Charm is a lie and beauty a fleeting breath, but a woman who fears the LORD — she will be praised.
20_31_31: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates.
57_1_1: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our dearly beloved friend and fellow worker,
57_1_2: and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your house:
57_1_3: May grace and peace be yours, from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
57_1_4: I thank my God always, making mention of you in my prayers,
57_1_5: because I hear of your love and of the faith you hold toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints.
57_1_6: And I pray that the sharing of your faith may become effective in the full knowledge of every good thing that is in us for Christ.
57_1_7: For I have found great joy and comfort in your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
57_1_8: For this reason, though in Christ I have full boldness to command you to do what is fitting,
57_1_9: yet for love's sake I would rather appeal to you — I, Paul, now an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus —
57_1_10: I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my chains —
57_1_11: who once was useless to you, but now has become useful indeed — to you and to me.
57_1_12: I am sending him back to you — and with him my very heart.
57_1_13: I would have been glad to keep him with me, that he might serve me in your place while I am in chains for the gospel,
57_1_14: but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness would not be by compulsion but of your own free will.
57_1_15: Perhaps this is why he was parted from you for a little while: that you might have him back forever —
57_1_16: no longer as a mere slave, but as more than a slave — a brother dearly loved, above all to me, yet how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
57_1_17: So if you count me a partner, receive him as you would receive me.
57_1_18: And if he has wronged you in any way, or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
57_1_19: I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it — not to mention that you owe me your very self besides.
57_1_20: Yes, brother, let me have this benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
57_1_21: Sure of your obedience, I am writing to you — knowing you will do even beyond what I ask.
57_1_22: And at the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be graciously given back to you.
57_1_23: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
57_1_24: and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who labor here at my side.
57_1_25: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with the spirit of each of you. Amen.
8_1_1: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine came over the land. So a certain man of Bethlehem in Judah set out to live for a while in the country of Moab — he and his wife and his two sons.
8_1_2: The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and his two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion — Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the country of Moab and settled there.
8_1_3: Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
8_1_4: They took for themselves Moabite wives — the name of one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth — and they lived there about ten years.
8_1_5: Then both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left bereft of her two children and of her husband — stripped of every man who should have provided for her.
8_1_6: So she set out with her daughters-in-law to return from the country of Moab, for she had heard there that the LORD had visited His people and given them bread.
8_1_7: She left the place where she had been living, her two daughters-in-law with her, and they went on their way to return to the land of Judah.
8_1_8: But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go back, each of you, to your mother's house. May the LORD show you covenant kindness, just as you have shown it to the dead and to me.
8_1_9: May the LORD grant that each of you find rest, a home in the house of a husband." Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.
8_1_10: But they said to her, "No — we will go back with you, to your own people."
8_1_11: Naomi said, "Turn back, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Do I have more sons in my womb who could become your husbands?
8_1_12: Turn back, my daughters; go your way, for I am too old to belong to a husband. Even if I said, 'I still have hope,' even if I had a husband tonight and bore sons —
8_1_13: would you wait for them until they were grown? Would you shut yourselves away from having husbands for them? No, my daughters. It grieves me deeply for your sakes, for the hand of the LORD has gone out against me."
8_1_14: Again they lifted up their voices and wept. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye — but Ruth clung to her.
8_1_15: "Look," said Naomi, "your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her gods. Go back, after your sister-in-law."
8_1_16: But Ruth said, "Do not urge or press me to leave you behind, or to turn back from following you. For wherever you go, I will go; and wherever you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
8_1_17: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD deal with me, be it ever so severely, if anything but death itself parts you from me."
8_1_18: When Naomi saw that Ruth was resolved to go with her, she said no more to dissuade her.
8_1_19: So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. And when they arrived, the whole town was stirred over them, and the women asked, "Can this be Naomi?"
8_1_20: "Do not call me Naomi," she told them. "Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
8_1_21: "I went out full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi, when the LORD has testified against me, and the Almighty has brought calamity upon me?"
8_1_22: So Naomi returned, and with her Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, who had come back from the country of Moab. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
8_2_1: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side — a man of standing and substance, from the family of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.
8_2_2: Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields and glean among the ears of grain behind anyone in whose eyes I find favor." And Naomi said to her, "Go, my daughter."
8_2_3: So she went out, and came and gleaned in the field behind the reapers; and as it happened, she came to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
8_2_4: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, "The LORD be with you." And they answered him, "The LORD bless you."
8_2_5: Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, "Whose young woman is this?"
8_2_6: The servant in charge of the reapers answered, "She is the Moabite girl who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.
8_2_7: She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.' So she came, and she has kept at it from morning until now, resting only a little in the shelter."
8_2_8: Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen, my daughter. Do not go to glean in another field; do not leave this one, but stay close here beside my young women.
8_2_9: Keep your eyes on the field they are reaping, and follow along after them. Have I not ordered the young men not to touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the jars and drink from what the young men have drawn."
8_2_10: Then she fell on her face, bowing to the ground, and said to him, "Why have I found such favor in your eyes, that you would take notice of me — and I only a foreigner?"
8_2_11: Boaz answered her, "It has been fully told to me — all that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband: how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people you did not know before.
8_2_12: May the LORD repay your deed, and may a full reward be given you by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."
8_2_13: And she said, "Let me keep finding favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your servant — though I am not even one of your servant women."
8_2_14: At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here, eat some bread, and dip your morsel in the sour wine." So she sat beside the reapers, and he passed her roasted grain. She ate and was satisfied, and had some left over.
8_2_15: When she rose to glean, Boaz ordered his young men, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not shame her.
8_2_16: And even pull out some stalks for her from the bundles on purpose, and leave them for her to glean — and do not rebuke her."
8_2_17: So she gleaned in the field until evening, and then beat out what she had gathered — and it came to about an ephah of barley.
8_2_18: She took it up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gleaned. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had left over after she was satisfied.
8_2_19: Her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you." So she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked: "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz."
8_2_20: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "May he be blessed by the LORD, whose covenant kindness has not forsaken the living or the dead." And Naomi added, "The man is a close relative of ours — one of our kinsman-redeemers."
8_2_21: Ruth the Moabitess said, "He even told me, 'Stay close by my young workers until they have finished all my harvest.'"
8_2_22: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that no one may harm you in another field."
8_2_23: So Ruth stayed close to the young women of Boaz, gleaning until the end of the barley and wheat harvests; and she lived with her mother-in-law.
8_3_1: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, where it will be well with you?
8_3_2: Now is not Boaz, with whose young women you have been, our kinsman? Look — tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.
8_3_3: So wash yourself, anoint yourself, put on your cloak, and go down to the threshing floor; but do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.
8_3_4: When he lies down, mark the place where he lies; then go, uncover his feet, and lie down. And he will tell you what to do."
8_3_5: And Ruth answered her, "I will do everything you have told me."
8_3_6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had told her.
8_3_7: When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was glad, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then she came softly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
8_3_8: In the middle of the night the man was startled; he turned over — and there was a woman lying at his feet!
8_3_9: "Who are you?" he asked. And she answered, "I am Ruth, your servant. Spread the corner of your garment over your servant, for you are a kinsman-redeemer."
8_3_10: And he said, "May you be blessed by the LORD, my daughter. You have shown more kindness now than at the first, by not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.
8_3_11: Now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you all that you ask, for all my people in the town gate know that you are a worthy woman.
8_3_12: Now it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer; yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.
8_3_13: Stay the night, and in the morning, if he will redeem you, good — let him redeem. But if he is not willing to redeem you, then as the LORD lives, I myself will redeem you. Lie down until morning."
8_3_14: So she lay at his feet until morning, and rose before anyone could recognize another; for he said, "Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
8_3_15: And he said, "Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out." So she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and laid it on her; then he went into the town.
8_3_16: When she came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" And Ruth told her all that the man had done for her.
8_3_17: And she said, "He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, 'Do not go back empty-handed to your mother-in-law.'"
8_3_18: Then Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you know how the matter turns out; for the man will not rest unless he settles it this very day."
8_4_1: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there. And just then the kinsman-redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken came by. Boaz said, "Come over here, friend, and sit down." So he turned aside and sat down.
8_4_2: Then Boaz took ten men of the elders of the town and said, "Sit down here." And they sat down.
8_4_3: And he said to the kinsman-redeemer, "Naomi, who has come back from the country of Moab, is selling the parcel of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
8_4_4: So I thought I would bring it to your attention and say: buy it back in the presence of those sitting here and of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if you will not, tell me, so I may know — for there is no one to redeem it but you, and I am after you." And he said, "I will redeem it."
8_4_5: Then Boaz said, "On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabitess, the widow of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance."
8_4_6: At that the kinsman-redeemer said, "Then I cannot redeem it for myself, or I would ruin my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption yourself, for I cannot redeem it."
8_4_7: Now this was the custom in earlier times in Israel concerning redemption and exchange: to confirm a matter, a man would take off his sandal and give it to the other; this was the manner of attesting in Israel.
8_4_8: So the kinsman-redeemer said to Boaz, "Buy it for yourself," and he drew off his sandal.
8_4_9: Then Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have bought from the hand of Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech, and all that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon.
8_4_10: And I have also acquired Ruth the Moabitess, the widow of Mahlon, to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, so that the name of the dead may not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his town. You are witnesses today."
8_4_11: Then all the people at the gate, and the elders, said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman coming into your house like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and be renowned in Bethlehem.
8_4_12: And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring the LORD will give you by this young woman."
8_4_13: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. And he went in to her, and the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.
8_4_14: Then the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who today has not let you go without a kinsman-redeemer! May his name be celebrated in Israel.
8_4_15: He will be to you a restorer of life and a sustainer of your old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you and is better to you than seven sons, has given him birth."
8_4_16: And Naomi took the child, laid him on her lap, and became his nurse.
8_4_17: And the women, her neighbors, gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." They named him Obed; he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
8_4_18: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron,
8_4_19: Hezron was the father of Ram, Ram the father of Amminadab,
8_4_20: Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmon,
8_4_21: Salmon the father of Boaz, Boaz the father of Obed,
8_4_22: Obed the father of Jesse, and Jesse the father of David.
